lines.text: What if these two cities fell? The map of Europe would change.
Kramatorsk and Sloviansk. They hold up Ukraine's whole defense in the east.
lines.say: Krah-ma-torsk and Slo-vyansk. They hold up Ukraine's whole defense in the east.

lines.text: Russia already took the towns around them, one by one.
Now it's fighting for Kostiantynivka, the gateway to the rest of the region.
lines.say: Now it's fighting for Kos-tyan-tee-niv-ka, the gateway to the rest of the region.

lines.text: Behind them, the map opens west.
Russian forces push toward the Dnipro, the river that runs down the middle of Ukraine.
To the south, the front already sits south-east of Zaporizhzhia city.
lines.say: To the south, the front already sits south-east of Za-po-rizh-zhya city.

lines.text: To the north, Kharkiv, Ukraine's second biggest city, sits thirty kilometers from Russia.
Ukraine is the biggest country entirely inside Europe.
Every line that moves here redraws the map of Europe.
This hasn't happened. Today, Russia holds about one fifth of Ukraine.
And two cities are holding the line.
